text:
Jakob Chychrun scored 26 goals last season, and the follow-up has been slow to start. He ended a goal drought on the power play this week (CBS Sports), and the same game produced the week's oddest highlight: RMNB on Alex Ovechkin pushing a bladeless Chychrun up the ice, hockey's version of the Tush Push.

The rest of his game is fine. He plays 24:29 a night, has 11 points in 15 games with six on the power play, and his 48 shots are the kind of volume that scored 26 last year. Two goals on 3.0 expected is a little unlucky, and shooting 4.2% is well below anything we'd expect from him. Washington has also scored fewer goals than its chances with him on. Evolving-Hockey had him 23rd among defensemen last season, built almost entirely on even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting to the slot more than most at his position. Our projection has 12 to 25 more goals. We'd trust the shots, not the start.
headline: Chychrun's goals should be coming
